sources.name: AIP Japan AD2.24 charts for RJBB / RJOO / RJBE (public mirror)
sources.notes: Publicly hosted copy of the official JCAB eAIP chart packages (info.json: EffectiveDate 2026-03-01, source URL aisjapan.mlit.go.jp eAIP 20260219/20260301). Individual RJBB pages EFF 20 MAR 2025 / 17 APR 2025 / 2 OCT 2025; RJOO pages EFF 2020-2026; RJBE EFF 20 MAR 2025. Primary source for all SID/STAR/approach legs, altitude/speed constraints, RNAV waypoint coordinates, frequencies, magnetic variation. Text extracted with pdftotext; some chart pages have scrambled coordinate tables, so coordinates were cross-checked (see notes).

sources.name: VATJPN TOKYO-ES EuroScope sector package (RJTG.sct / RJTG.ese)
sources.notes: Community (VATSIM Japan) sector file, Navigraph/AIP-derived, last pushed 2025-06. Used for VOR/TACAN coordinates and frequencies, fix coordinates, airway segments (LOW/HIGH AIRWAY sections already contain the 2025 Kansai reorganisation routes Y34/Y35/Y36/Y53/Y236/Y542/Y544), and as a cross-check of SID/STAR fix sequences (SIDSSTARS section).

magVar.note: AIP Japan: VAR 8degW (2023), annual change ~5'W; RNAV leg coding uses -8.1 at RJBB, -8.0 at RJOO, -8.2 at RJBE. Older RJOO conventional charts still print 7degW (2007).

notes:
HOW THE KANSAI SYSTEM WORKS (from AIP 2025/26 charts):
- KIX (RJBB) has two parallel runways, 06R/24L (runway A, original island, eastern) and 06L/24R (runway B, 2nd island, western). Elev 17 ft. Prevailing configuration is RWY24 (south-westerly flow); RWY06 for north-easterly winds. Approach is KANSAI APP 120.25/125.5, TWR 118.2/118.05, ATIS 127.85.
- Since 20 MAR 2025 KIX arrivals use RNP1 STARs named after the entry fix + a letter. Entry fixes: DUBKA (east, Kii peninsula - traffic from Kanto/Nagoya via Y544 KOHWA-SINGU-RIDGE-DUBKA), EVERT (south/Pacific, Y46/Y48 international arrivals), NIXOV (south-west, Y53 from Okinawa/SE Asia), CANDY (south-west, Kochi side), IGLEV (west, Y35 from Kyushu), ATMUG (north-west, Y36 from Hiroshima/Okayama/Korea). Letters: A = short RWY06 routes (to BERRY/AVDOX/ATVID), B = RWY06 point-merge style arcs (BB650-652 / BB653-655 / BB656-659) at 10000-12000ft, 230kt; C/D/E = RWY24 routes ending at MAYAH; M = RWY24 point-merge arcs (BB460-463 / BB464-466 / BB467-470) feeding NOBUN-AWAJI-LILAC-SAPEK-MAYAH. Conventional SASVO and TOKUSHIMA (TSC-GATES) arrivals also exist.
- RWY24 flow: all arrivals converge on MAYAH (north of KIX over Osaka Bay, 4000ft), then MAYAH-ONEGU(2600, max 185kt)-OSNIT-BB452(2000)-OPARU(1600) = a right-hand base turning onto final from the north-east (24R IF OPARU / FAF BEBIL; 24L via AMBER / FAF AMEZY). Alternative ILS Y uses the KIE 10.9DME arc from MAYAH. RWY06 flow: arrivals end at BERRY / ATVID / AVDOX (south-west of KIX, 4000ft) then MIBIB (2500) and a 059deg final (FAF ~4NM at 1300ft); ILS Y/X 06 are long straight-ins from GATES (Tokushima side).
- KIX departures: MAIKO-bound (MAIKO1/FERRY7 conventional, RINKU1/IWAYA3 RNAV) then west transitions (OLIVE/KTE/SHION/SOUJA/WASYU/HABAR); TOMOH-bound south (TOMOH4/TOMOH WEST2 conventional, SUSAN3 RNAV; KOCHI/KUSHIMOTO/DOPDA transitions); UPMIN1 south (DOPDA/IVROG); SOVRI1 east (UPRAL/SHTLE toward Nagoya/Tokyo); NANKO3 north-east (GUJYO/Nagoya); LINDA1 west (SHION/WASYU/HABAR); OBLUR1 and OMGOR1 south-west. Departures generally climb on runway heading to 500ft (5% gradient) before turning. ESE (VATJPN) assigns all SIDs to all four runways.
- ITM (RJOO): RWY 32L/14R (3000m) and 32R/14L (1828m). Normal flow is RWY32 for landing: all arrivals funnel to IKOMA (3500ft, south-east of ITM near Mt Ikoma) via IZUMI / AGPUK / IKOMA EAST / IKOMA NORTH / HABIK STARs, then ILS 32L (IF IKOMA, FAF MIDOH 3500, course 322) or RNP 32L/32R. There is no instrument approach to RWY14 (ITM is in a dense urban area; RWY14 arrivals are circling/visual). Departures: TIGER2 (west), IZUMI1 (south), ASUKA4/PANAS1/MINAC4 (east), EAST REVERSAL4. ITM airspace sits beneath/inside the Kansai TCA; KANSAI APP 120.45/124.7 serves ITM.
- UKB (RJBE): single RWY09/27 on an island in Kobe harbour. Arrivals via OMBIP/KAGAWA (conventional) and AVKUL/TRACY (RNP) to SIOJI (3000ft) for ILS/RNP RWY09 (LOC 109.15 IKO, course 092). Departures: KOBE6 (to MAIKO) and MUKRI1 RNP (TARUP-LEMET-MUKRI) with transitions west/north.
- Holding: RNAV holds at MAYAH-area fixes; typical KIX holds LILAC (3000, inbound 057), GATES (4000), SASVO (4000), DUBKA (8000-10000), IGLEV (11000-12000), ATMUG (10000), CANDY/NIXOV (9000-10000). Speed limits in holds: 230kt at/below FL140, 240kt above.
- Magnetic variation: AIP RNAV coding uses -8.1 (KIX), -8.0 (ITM), -8.2 (UKB); charts state VAR 8degW (2023), annual change ~5'W. Some older RJOO conventional charts still show 7degW (2007 epoch).

COORDINATE QUALITY:
- 179 fixes have coordinates taken directly from the AIP chart text and agree with the VATJPN/Navigraph-derived sector file (136 full lat/lon pairs, 37 matched via separate lat/lon tokens), plus 7 AIP-only points (B6R62, B6R63, BE950, O2L53, RW32L, RW32R, RW09). Every procedure fix used here was additionally validated by computing great-circle leg lengths and comparing with the AIP-published leg distances (about 150 legs, all within 0.3NM / 3%).
- Remaining fixes (mostly airway points far from Kansai) come from the VATJPN sector file only (AIP-derived community data, AIRAC ~2023-2025) and were not individually checked against AIP.
- Navaid coordinates/frequencies are from the sector file; frequencies of KIE, ITE, KCE, YOE, KEC, TSC, KTE, KRE, OYE, YME, KCC, CBE, KMC are confirmed on AIP charts.

GAPS / CAVEATS:
- No NDBs: none remain in the Kansai area (the sector file lists none, and current AIP charts reference none). Akashi / Shinsei / Shirahama VORs do not exist under those names; the Shirahama area facility is NANKI (NKE). AWAJI (AJD, CH-103X) and SHODO (STD, CH-91X) are DME-only facilities shown on ITM charts; their coordinates were not found, so they are omitted.
- Conventional SID/STAR legs defined by radials/DME (e.g. KCE R215/41.0DME, ITE R141/19.0DME, D-points) are described in 'note' but not encoded as legs because they have no published name/coordinate.
- Some approach intermediate altitudes were read from chart profile text that extracts poorly (ILS/RNP Z 06R OTBON 1600, 24L/24R OSNIT/BB452/OPARU values, RJOO LOC 32L NATEN, RJBE BE950 1606); these are flagged in each approach note. FAF altitudes and glidepath data are clear.
- Localizer courses are given magnetic as printed (06L/06R 059, 24L 238, 24R 239, RJOO 32L 322, RJBE 09 092); true courses are approx magnetic - 8.1.
- Airways come from the sector file segment lists, chained automatically and cropped to 31-37N / 131-140.6E; direction restrictions, MEA/MOCA and conditional routes are not encoded. A few airway point orders could reflect segment ordering in the file rather than published direction.
- RJOO SID 'EAST REVERSAL4' is encoded only as ITE (assigned altitude); RJOO STARs IZUMI/AGPUK are also usable for RWY14 circling per ESE but AIP lists no runway restriction.
- Procedure 'type' (conventional / rnav / transition) and loc fields (locIdent/locFreq) are extra keys beyond the requested schema.
